exposure: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) diagnosis timing (late pregnancy vs. after birth)
cohort: 328 women carrying a single infant with an estimated fetal weight below the tenth percentile
finding: While a prenatal diagnosis of late-onset FGR is associated with higher intervention and preterm birth rates compared to a diagnosis made after birth, after adjusting for confounders, there was no difference in the composite adverse neonatal outcome between groups.
